A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable, ten-page versions of the same StreamFlow work. Their text, equations, algorithms, figures, tables, and references support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original throughput, power, memory, scalability, ablation, and generation-quality measurements in Figures 4–5 and Tables 1–2.

after.justification: Section 4 retains the original StreamFlow experiments and their measured outcomes in Figures 4–5 and Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: The batched velocity-field scheduler, heterogeneous-timestep pipeline, and adaptive TensorRT procedure in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–3 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same text-to-image and img2img scenarios, including generation across resolutions from 64 to 1024 pixels. The quality benchmarks remain unnamed in both versions; no dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The Hugging Face pipeline and vanilla PeRFlow baseline remain in the corresponding comparisons. The Xformer, TensorRT, VAE, and component configurations also match across Figures 4–5 and Tables 1–2.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains timing averaged over 100 images, default four-step generation at 512×512, the same configuration sweeps, and the same FPS, power, memory, CLIP Score, and FID metrics.

E4.justification: Figure 4 retains the same component, inference-step, decoder-batch, and generation-mode ablations. Figure 5 retains the same resolution scalability analysis; no robustness test or case study is added.

E5.justification: The 100-image timing average is reported identically. Neither version provides independent repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The experimental pages and their numerical and qualitative results are identical. Table 1 retains 10.05 FPS for tensorrt+taesd+VFB, versus 2.22 for the Hugging Face baseline and 1.87 for the vanilla baseline. Table 2 retains CLIP Score 96.25 and FID 31.28 for that TensorRT configuration.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, the complexity analysis, and the throughput derivation are unchanged. Replacing 'Eq. ??' with 'Eq. 4' in Section 3.1.3 repairs a cross-reference without revising mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same three-component framework, novelty positioning, claimed acceleration up to 611%, and claims of largely preserved generation quality.

C2.justification: The introduction drops v1's assertion that denoising has a minimum basic unit when explaining misalignment from variable-length flow timesteps. This slightly narrows the mechanistic comparison. The experimental interpretations, compatibility trade-off, and applicability claims remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Hardware and operating-system specifications, scheduler and pipeline pseudocode, TensorRT runtime details, and the project-page link are unchanged. No implementation or resource-access information is added.

R1.justification: The Inference Acceleration passage and bibliography remove SignDiff (Fang et al., 2025c). SignX receives updated bibliographic details but retains arXiv identifier 2504.16315, so it is not a newly cited work. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Short introductory passages are rewritten to clarify pipeline queues and scheduling challenges, TensorRT capitalization is standardized, and the broken equation reference is repaired. Yanxin Zhang is added to the author list, with affiliation, date, and bibliography edits. Section organization is unchanged.

P2.justification: All five figures, two tables, and three algorithm displays remain unchanged. Author-list and prose edits cause limited text reflow, while the shortened bibliography shifts references between columns and pages 9–10.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves readability and navigation by tightening introductory explanations and replacing the unresolved equation reference in Section 3.1.3 with Eq. 4. These are limited editorial gains; the method, empirical evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
